text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Philips has scrapped 25,000 jobs since Cor Boonstra took over as chairman last October, 5,500 in the Netherlands and 19,500 in other countries. (p1)
- The number of fraud cases at banks and insurers much higher than thought. Some 4,300 cases a year are recommended for further investigation (p1).
- Measures to be brought in after 2000 to cut down car emissions might cost 1.3 billion guilders (p1).
- Dutch private health insurers are opposed to the creation of a single national health insurance scheme as proposed by a Dutch government advisory body (p1).
- KLM has not informed the passengers reported to have been at risk from radioactive freight. (p1)
- Dutch government coalition partner the Labour party wants an end to event sponsorship by cigarette and drinks companies (p1).
- U.S. President Bill Clinton sees the Netherlands' "Polder Model" is an economic success story and one that deserves attention and further consideration (p1).
- Business optimism in the developed world is near historically high levels. Dutch business community lags a little in optimism but above European average. (p13).
- Sportsshoes and sportswear chain Coach ready to set up shops abroad. (p13)
- Study shows a change in Dutch strategic policy on airfreight could create an extra 150,000 jobs in the next 25 years. (p13)
- Agricultural ministry prohibits pig farmers from moving their businesses to Groningen and Zeeland
